es.summary: Serie de reacciones enzimáticas que convierten la sangre líquida en un coágulo estable para detener el sangrado.
key_points: Hemostasia primaria: adhesión y agregación plaquetaria formando tapón plaquetario.
Hemostasia secundaria: cascada de coagulación que genera fibrina a partir de fibrinógeno.
Vías intrínseca y extrínseca convergen en la vía común, activando la trombina.
La trombina convierte fibrinógeno en fibrina y activa más plaquetas.
Pruebas de laboratorio: PT (vía extrínseca), aPTT (vía intrínseca), INR (monitor de warfarina).
Factores dependientes de vitamina K (II, VII, IX, X) son esenciales para la coagulación.

purpose: Comprender los mecanismos de hemostasia y coagulación.
Diferenciar la hemostasia primaria de la secundaria.
Identificar factores clave y pruebas de laboratorio.
procedure: Lesión vascular → exposición de colágeno y factor von Willebrand.
Adhesión plaquetaria mediante GPIb y GPIIb/IIIa.
Activación plaquetaria y liberación de ADP y TXA2.
Iniciación de la cascada: vía extrínseca (factor VII) y vía intrínseca (factores XII, XI, IX, VIII).
Convergencia en la vía común: activación del factor X, formación de protrombinasa, generación de trombina.
Conversión de fibrinógeno a fibrina, estabilización del coágulo y retracción.
safety: Monitorear signos de sangrado activo (hematomas, hematuria, melena).
Verificar resultados de PT, aPTT, INR antes de procedimientos invasivos.
Evitar medicamentos que alteren la función plaquetaria sin orden médica.
Mantener registro de uso de anticoagulantes y suplementos de vitamina K.
nursing_care: Evaluar presión arterial, frecuencia cardíaca y signos de hipotensión.
Inspeccionar sitio de lesión y mucosas en busca de sangrado.
Controlar laboratorios de coagulación cada 24‑48 h según indicación.
Reportar aumento del PT/aPTT, sangrado inesperado o petequias al médico.
documentation: Fecha y hora de la evaluación de sangrado.
Resultados de PT, aPTT, INR y valores de factores de coagulación.
Intervenciones realizadas y respuesta del paciente.
Educación al paciente sobre signos de alarma y manejo de anticoagulantes.

outcomes: Control del sangrado: sin evidencia de hemorragia activa en 24 h.
Nivel de hemoglobina: mantener ≥12 g/dL durante la hospitalización.

interventions.action: Evaluar signos de sangrado cada 4 h y registrar resultados.
Monitorear PT, aPTT e INR según orden médica.
interventions.rationale: Los valores guían la necesidad de ajustar anticoagulantes.

interventions.action: Mantener el sitio de venopunción con compresión adecuada.
Educar al paciente sobre evitar actividades que aumenten riesgo de lesión.
interventions.rationale: Reduce la probabilidad de traumatismos que provoquen sangrado.

interventions.action: Administrar suplementos de vitamina K solo bajo prescripción.
interventions.rationale: Corrige deficiencias que pueden prolongar la coagulación.

en.summary: Series of enzymatic reactions that convert liquid blood into a stable clot to stop bleeding.
key_points: Primary hemostasis: platelet adhesion and aggregation forming a platelet plug.
Secondary hemostasis: coagulation cascade generating fibrin from fibrinogen.
Intrinsic and extrinsic pathways converge on the common pathway, activating thrombin.
Thrombin converts fibrinogen to fibrin and activates more platelets.
Laboratory tests: PT (extrinsic pathway), aPTT (intrinsic pathway), INR (warfarin monitoring).
Vitamin K–dependent factors (II, VII, IX, X) are essential for coagulation.

purpose: Understand the mechanisms of hemostasis and coagulation.
Identify key factors and laboratory tests.
procedure: Vascular injury → exposure of collagen and von Willebrand factor.
Platelet adhesion via GPIb and GPIIb/IIIa.
Platelet activation and release of ADP and TXA2.
Initiation of the cascade: extrinsic pathway (factor VII) and intrinsic pathway (factors XII, XI, IX, VIII).
Convergence on the common pathway: activation of factor X, formation of prothrombinase, generation of thrombin.
Conversion of fibrinogen to fibrin, clot stabilization and contraction.
safety: Monitor for active bleeding signs (hematomas, hematuria, melena).
Verify PT, aPTT, INR results before invasive procedures.
Avoid medications that alter platelet function without medical order.
Maintain records of anticoagulant use and vitamin K supplements.
nursing_care: Assess blood pressure, heart rate, and signs of hypotension.
Inspect injury site and mucous membranes for bleeding.
Monitor coagulation labs every 24‑48 h as indicated.
Report increased PT/aPTT, unexpected bleeding, or petechiae to the physician.
documentation: Date and time of bleeding assessment.
PT, aPTT, INR results and coagulation factor values.
Patient education on warning signs and anticoagulant management.

outcomes: Bleeding control: no evidence of active hemorrhage within 24 h.
Hemoglobin level: maintain ≥12 g/dL during hospitalization.

interventions.action: Assess bleeding signs every 4 h and record findings.
Monitor PT, aPTT, and INR as ordered.
interventions.rationale: Values guide the need to adjust anticoagulants.

interventions.action: Maintain venipuncture site with adequate compression.
Educate patient to avoid activities that increase injury risk.
interventions.rationale: Reduces the likelihood of trauma that causes bleeding.

interventions.action: Administer vitamin K supplements only under prescription.
interventions.rationale: Corrects deficiencies that may prolong coagulation.

sources.name: Pharmacology for Nurses: Introduction to Clotting and Coagulation

summary.0.quote: This process is supported by complex cascade of enzymatic reactions and essential proteins that combine to form a stable blood clot.

key_points.0.quote: Primary hemostasis is the process of platelet adhesion to form a platelet plug, or platelets that are aggregated on the injured vessel wall or tissues.

key_points.3.quote: Thrombin facilitates the activation of fibrinogen to fibrin.

key_points.5.quote: Vitamin K, a vitamin present in foods such as green, leafy vegetables, is a cofactor needed for synthesis of clotting factors II, VII, IX, and X.

sections.purpose.0.quote: To effectively treat thrombotic disorders, nurses must understand the complex mechanisms of coagulation , which is the process of a liquid changing into a semi-solid or solid state.

sections.purpose.1.quote: Primary hemostasis is the process of platelet adhesion to form a platelet plug, or platelets that are aggregated on the injured vessel wall or tissues.

sections.purpose.2.quote: Other laboratory work is slower but can include clotting factors, CBC count, PT, PTT, and INR.

sections.procedure.0.quote: Platelets can be activated in response to collagen released during tissue damage or by a number of other substances.

sections.procedure.2.quote: Figure 20.2 Platelet activation occurs through thromboxane A2, adenosine diphosphate, thrombin, von Willebrand’s factor, and fibrinogen, among other substances.
